label: Financial runway
summary: Financial runway is the cushion of saved money that makes it practically possible to leave a stable income behind. In Maaike's work it appears as the concrete, material side of an exit strategy: you need enough money set aside to survive a period without any income before you can seriously consider going independent. It is less a planning concept and more a precondition.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike built her financial runway deliberately by putting herself on a minimal salary, cutting back on non-essentials, and saving everything left over into what she called an emergency exit account. Her specific target was enough money to survive one full year without income, which she treated as the threshold at which the leap into freelance work became realistic rather than reckless. She frames this not as financial advice but as a personal and psychological process: reducing her salary also helped her detach from the status and identity she had tied to corporate earnings.
open_questions: The passage cuts off before describing what happened once the financial runway was actually used, so it is unclear how the one-year target held up in practice.
Maaike mentions COVID had an impact on her freelance journey but does not explain whether or how that affected her financial runway.
